issues.legal_issue: A reasoned dismissal of the acquiring authority’s special leave petition makes the compensation award final against that authority but does not bar the landholders’ pending appeal seeking enhancement.
material_facts: The acquiring authority’s special leave petition challenging the compensation awarded by the High Court was dismissed by a reasoned order.
The landholders had appeared in that proceeding but could not advance their own arguments seeking enhanced compensation.
The landholders’ review proceedings in the High Court were still pending when the authority’s petition was dismissed, and the landholders later pursued their own appeals.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal of the acquiring authority’s special leave petition did not prevent the landholders from pursuing their appeals for enhancement; the authority could not obtain a further reduction of the compensation already awarded.
issues.legal_principle: A reasoned dismissal of a special leave petition results in merger of the lower court’s judgment in the Supreme Court’s order, making that decision final as against the petitioner. It does not decide a different party’s claim for relief that the party could not advance in that proceeding and was still pursuing. The Court applied the principles in Kunhayammed v. State of Kerala and S. Gangadhara Palo v. Revenue Divisional Officer.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.acquiring_authority_slp_dismissed_with_r: The acquiring authority’s special leave petition challenging the compensation award was dismissed with reasons.
predicates.landholders_could_not_seek_enhancement_i: The landholders participated in the authority’s special leave proceeding but could not seek enhancement of their own compensation there.
predicates.landholders_enhancement_claim_still_pend: The landholders’ own claim for enhanced compensation remained pending when the authority’s special leave petition was decided.

issues.definition: When an acquiring authority’s reasoned challenge is dismissed while the landholders’ separate enhancement claim remains pending and could not be advanced in that challenge, the authority’s challenge is final but the landholders’ appeal remains open.

issues.legal_issue: Averaging prices from multiple comparable sales is permissible when the sales concern similar land in the same locality and period and their prices vary within a narrow range.
material_facts: The landholders relied on four plot transactions in the same residential scheme, executed shortly before the acquisition notification.
The plots were smaller than the acquired land, but the High Court treated the transactions as comparable and made deductions for the difference in plot size and development.
The Court found the transactions related to the same locality and a sufficiently close period, with prices showing only marginal variation.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was justified in averaging the four comparable prices; it was not required to select only the highest price.
issues.legal_principle: Market value is ordinarily assessed by comparing bona fide open-market transactions near the valuation date involving land with similar situation and advantages. The highest bona fide comparable sale is usually considered, but an average may be used where several sales concern similar land and their prices fall within a narrow range. Averaging is inappropriate for dissimilar lands or markedly different prices. The Court relied on Section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, Viluben Jhalejar Contractor v. State of Gujarat, State of Punjab v. Hans Raj, and Anjani Molu Dessai v. State of Goa.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and multiple_comparable_sales and sales_are_similar_and_near_in_time_and_location and prices_vary_narrowly

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.multiple_comparable_sales: More than one transaction is relied on to estimate the acquired land’s market value.
predicates.sales_are_similar_and_near_in_time_and_l: The transactions concern land with similar characteristics in the same or nearby locality and occurred close to the valuation date.
predicates.prices_vary_narrowly: The prices in the comparable transactions differ only marginally rather than being markedly different.

issues.definition: When an acquisition-compensation appeal involves multiple similar, nearby and timely sales whose prices vary narrowly, averaging their prices is permissible.

issues.legal_issue: Freehold land acquired without encumbrances may warrant an upward adjustment when its comparable sales are of leasehold land.
material_facts: The acquired land was freehold, while the relied-on plot transactions were perpetual leasehold interests.
A leaseholder seeking to convert a perpetual leasehold interest to freehold had to pay an additional amount.
The High Court’s valuation did not account for the difference between the leasehold comparables and the acquired freehold land.
issues.conclusion: An upward adjustment was appropriate to account for the acquired land’s freehold status; the Court added 20% to the averaged comparable price before making other deductions.
issues.legal_principle: Freehold and leasehold interests are distinct. A private purchaser of property subject to a lease may offer less because the purchaser obtains an encumbered interest, whereas land acquired free from encumbrances has a higher market value. The Court distinguished the encumbrance principle discussed in M.B. Gopala Krishna v. Special Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition, and held that the leasehold comparables and the need to pay for conversion supported an adjustment in this case.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and acquired_interest_is_freehold and comparable_sales_are_leasehold and conversion_to_freehold_requires_payment

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.acquired_interest_is_freehold: The acquired property is held as a freehold interest rather than a leasehold interest.
predicates.comparable_sales_are_leasehold: The transactions used as comparables concern leasehold interests.
predicates.conversion_to_freehold_requires_payment: A holder of the comparable leasehold interest must pay an additional amount to convert it to freehold.

issues.definition: When freehold acquired land is valued by reference to leasehold comparables that require payment for conversion, an upward adjustment for freehold status is warranted.

issues.legal_issue: Prices from auction sales may require a deduction to account for competitive bidding when they are used to value acquired land.
material_facts: The comparable plot transactions were auction transactions conducted by a public authority.
The plots were in a developed layout, while the acquired land was a large tract of undeveloped land.
The Court found that competitive bidding could elevate auction prices above ordinary market value.
issues.conclusion: The Court applied a deduction for competitive bidding to the auction prices before using them to value the acquired land.
issues.legal_principle: Auction prices are not automatically reliable measures of market value because competition among bidders may inflate them. Where an auction sale is a relevant comparable, a suitable deduction may be made to offset the competitive price increase. The Court relied on Executive Engineer, Karnataka Housing Board v. Land Acquisition Officer, Gadag and Raj Kumar v. Haryana State.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.comparable_transactions_are_auctions: The transactions relied on as comparables resulted from auctions.
predicates.auction_competition_may_have_inflated_pr: The auction process involved competition capable of raising prices above ordinary market value.

issues.definition: When auction transactions are used as comparables in an acquisition-compensation appeal and competition may have inflated their prices, a deduction for competitive bidding is warranted.

issues.legal_issue: Deductions from developed-plot prices used to value a large tract must separately account for land set aside for common facilities and the cost of development.
material_facts: The acquired land was a large tract to be developed under a planned residential scheme.
The comparable plots were small and situated in a developed layout.
The Court considered the land required for roads, drains, parks and civic amenities, as well as the costs of roads, drainage, sewerage and electricity works.
The Court calculated a total development deduction of 60%, producing a value below the amount already awarded by the High Court.
The acquiring authority’s challenge to the High Court’s award had already been dismissed, and the Court declined to reduce that award further.
issues.conclusion: The Court treated development deductions as comprising separate deductions for land used for layout and common facilities and for development costs. Although its calculation produced a lower value than the High Court’s award, it maintained the High Court’s compensation rather than reducing it further.
issues.legal_principle: For undeveloped or underdeveloped land valued by comparison with small developed plots, deductions may be required both for the area used for roads and common facilities and for the cost of development works. The amount depends on the land’s nature and location, the layout, the required facilities and the development already present. The Court relied on Section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, Haryana State Agricultural Market Board v. Krishan Kumar, Sabhia Mohammed Yusuf Abdul Hamid Mulla v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, Kasturi v. State of Haryana, and Lal Chand v. Union of India. It also relied on the finality of the acquiring authority’s dismissed challenge in declining to reduce the existing award.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and large_undeveloped_tract_compared_with_small_developed_plots and planned_layout_requires_common_facilities and development_work_is_required

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.large_undeveloped_tract_compared_with_sm: A large tract of undeveloped or underdeveloped land is valued using sales of small developed plots.
predicates.planned_layout_requires_common_facilitie: The intended layout requires land to be set aside for roads, drains, parks or other common facilities.
predicates.development_work_is_required: Work such as levelling, roads, drainage, sewerage or utility installation is required to develop the land.

issues.definition: When a large undeveloped tract is valued from small developed plots and both common facilities and development work are required, deductions account separately for the land used and the development costs.

issues.legal_issue: Statutory interest on compensation and interest on enhanced compensation are distinct, and a claimant is not entitled to interest again when both have already been awarded.
material_facts: The reference court confirmed the Collector’s compensation award and stated that statutory interest was payable.
The High Court enhanced the compensation and awarded interest on the enhanced amount from the relevant possession-related period, at the applicable rates.
The landholders nevertheless argued that interest on the enhanced compensation had been omitted.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the claim that interest remained unpaid because statutory interest and interest on the enhanced compensation had both been awarded.
issues.legal_principle: Section 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, makes interest on compensation mandatory from the taking of possession until payment or deposit. Section 28 empowers a court enhancing compensation to award interest on the excess amount, ordinarily from the taking of possession until payment or deposit. The Court relied on Gurpreet Singh v. Union of India and the principles in Prem Nath Kapur v. National Fertilizers Corporation of India.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.original_award_interest_granted: The claimant has been awarded statutory interest on the compensation determined in the original award.
predicates.enhanced_compensation_interest_granted: The claimant has also been awarded interest on the amount by which compensation was enhanced.

issues.definition: When a claimant in an acquisition-compensation appeal has already received interest on both the original compensation and the enhanced amount, a claim that interest on that compensation remains unpaid is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant who succeeds in part and fails in part may be awarded proportionate costs rather than all claimed costs and court fees.
material_facts: The landholders succeeded before the High Court in obtaining enhanced compensation but did not obtain the full compensation they had claimed.
The High Court awarded proportionate costs in addition to a fixed costs amount.
The landholders sought reimbursement of all court fees and the full costs associated with their claim.
issues.conclusion: The High Court acted properly in awarding proportionate costs, and the landholders were not entitled to recover all claimed costs and court fees.
issues.legal_principle: Section 27 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, gives the court power to determine by whom and in what proportions costs are to be paid. Section 35 of the Code of Civil Procedure may also be considered. Ordinarily, a litigant who succeeds in part and fails in part receives proportionate costs, and the court’s discretion will not be disturbed absent improper exercise.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.claimant_succeeds_in_part_and_fails_in_p: The claimant obtains some relief but does not obtain the full relief sought.
predicates.court_awards_proportionate_costs: The court allocates costs proportionately to the claimant’s degree of success.

issues.definition: When a claimant in an acquisition-compensation appeal obtains only partial relief and the court allocates costs proportionately, the claimant is not entitled as of right to all claimed costs and court fees.
